extracted.intended_audience: distributors/editors of Project Gutenberg works; transcribers; legal agents and officials handling restoration of kidnapped citizens; historians/researchers
extracted.subtask_description: Preparation, distribution, and archival presentation of a public-domain memoir as an electronic book (Project Gutenberg edition), plus the accompanying legal/procedural documents (memorials, affidavits, gubernatorial commissions) demonstrating statutory procedures for restoring kidnapped free citizens. Covers editorial corrections, licensing and redistribution rules, and the legal steps by which a state appoints an agent and effects restoration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governor's duty under Chap. 375 (trigger for action)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever the Governor shall receive information satisfactory to him that any free citizen or inhabitant of this State has been kidnapped or transported out of this State for the purpose of being held in slavery, or is wrongfully seized or held in slavery on the pretence that such person is a slave, it shall be the duty of the Governor to take such measures as he shall deem necessary to procure such person to be restored to his liberty and returned to this State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Governor must assess whether received information is satisfactory, and if so act; this statutory duty is the legal trigger for appointing agents and initiating recovery measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governor's authority to appoint agents and define commission
rubrics_metrics.description: The Governor is authorized to appoint and employ such agent or agents as he shall deem necessary to effect the restoration and return of such person; and shall furnish the said agent with such credentials and instructions as will be likely to accomplish the object of his appointment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Governor may determine the agent's compensation and provide credentials and instructions; the commission empowers the agent to pursue necessary legal measures and to travel to the relevant jurisdiction (e.g., Louisiana).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent responsibilities under Chap. 375
rubrics_metrics.description: Such agent shall proceed to collect the proper proof to establish the right of such person to his freedom, and shall perform such journeys, take such measures, institute and procure to be prosecuted such legal proceedings, under the direction of the Governor, as shall be necessary to procure such person to be restored to his liberty and returned to this State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agent must gather documentary and testimonial proof, bring or initiate legal proceedings, retain counsel if needed, and act under the Governor's direction to secure the person's release and return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accounting and payment procedures for agent expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: The accounts for all services and expenses incurred in carrying this act into effect shall be audited by the Comptroller, and paid by the Treasurer on his warrant, out of any moneys in the treasury not otherwise appropriated. The Treasurer may advance reasonable sums on certificate of the Governor, for which the agent must later account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fiscal oversight: agents' expenses are subject to audit and formal state payment processes; advances require accounting on final audit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memorial content requirements (example of Anne's memorial)
rubrics_metrics.description: A memorial (petition) should set forth the memorialist's identity, relationship to the missing person, key dates (age, marriage, residence history), the facts known about the alleged kidnapping (letters, postmarks, dates, locations), assertions that the missing person is a free citizen of the State, family circumstances (dependents, poverty), and a respectful request that the Governor employ an agent under the enabling statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Memorials should provide specific factual details sufficient to persuade the Governor that intervention is warranted; they are strengthened by sworn attestations and corroborating documentary evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sworn affidavits/witness statements as supporting proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Witnesses should provide sworn depositions before a justice (or appropriate official) attesting to facts such as long acquaintance, birthplace, continuous residence in the State, family history (parents' status), marriage dates, literacy, character of the memorialist, and belief that the missing person is wrongly held as a slave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affidavits must be signed, subscribed and sworn before a competent official (Justice of the Peace, Recorder), and should provide particulars (dates, places, relationships) to corroborate the memorial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governor's commission form and powers (appointment letter)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Governor's commission constitutes, appoints and employs an agent with full power to effect restoration, authorizing the agent to institute proper and legal proceedings, procure evidence, retain counsel, and take such measures as are likely to accomplish restoration; it may include travel instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The commission should be signed, sealed, and delivered; it functions as the agent's authority in the foreign jurisdiction to act on behalf of the State and the wronged citizen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local legal acknowledgment and surrender procedures (Louisiana certificate)
rubrics_metrics.description: A local official (e.g., Recorder) may execute a certificate acknowledging that, by virtue of the state's agent's commission and the proofs produced, the slaveholder surrenders the person to the agent for restoration; the surrender should be witnessed and recorded in official records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper execution requires signatures of agent and owner, presence of competent witnesses, and recording/certification by the local recorder to create a formal, recordable transfer of custody back to the agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcriber's editorial transparency and errata (transcriber's notes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transcriber documents all changes made to the original text (typographical corrections, emendations, punctuation adjustments) in a list of 'Transcriber's Notes' specifying page, original error, and correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing a modern electronic edition from older print, provide an explicit errata/changes list so readers know what was corrected; preserve meaning and indicate any substantive editorial choices.
